pr_title: Increase update interval in AccuWeather integration

<!--

AccuWeather allows 50 requests a day so users who frequently restart HA receive the error `The allowed number of requests has been exceeded`. Unfortunately, the moment of resetting the number of allowed requests is variable and we cannot calculate the dynamic update interval.
This PR increase `update_interval` for 40 minutes and 80 minutes if forecast is enabled.

issue_context.body:

  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Trying to setup a new integration I had to restart Home Assistant frequently after making changes to the configuration files. In the end I noticed the following message in my logs:
```txt
2020-10-21 16:34:33 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.config_entries] Config entry for accuweather not ready yet. Retrying in 80 seconds
2020-10-21 16:35:53 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.accuweather] Error fetching accuweather data: The allowed number of requests has been exceeded
```

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->
```
# ha core info

audio_input: null
audio_output: null

ip_address: 172.30.32.1

port: 8123

version: 0.116.4
version_latest: 0.116.4

watchdog: true
```
- Integration causing this issue: accuweater

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->
N/A

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
2020-10-21 16:34:33 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.config_entries] Config entry for accuweather not ready yet. Retrying in 80 seconds
2020-10-21 16:35:53 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.accuweather] Error fetching accuweather data: The allowed number of requests has been exceeded
```

## Additional information
comments: It seems a restart consumes one request of the AccuWeater API when setting up Home Assistant, is this really required? Could the requests of the integration be devided and equally distributed over the remaining time and (estimated/tracked) remaining requests?

Hey there @bieniu, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`accuweather`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L17) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

AccuWeather servers don't reset the number of available requests at a fixed time, so there is no easy way to calculate the appropriate update interval to ensure that the requests limit will not be exceeded. This is a limitation of the free AccuWeather API key.
If you need to restart the HA frequently, you must use other weather integration.

> AccuWeather servers don't reset the number of available requests at a fixed time, so there is no easy way to calculate the appropriate update interval to ensure that the requests limit will not be exceeded. This is a limitation of the free AccuWeather API key.

Fair enough but from the data obtained from the message and error count of last 24 hours I am able to deduce the number of allowed requests per 24h (293 messages - 243 errors = **_50 successful requests_**, although at some times I am able to perform 8 per hour). The number of requests could be tracked per 24h, compared to the remaining time frame and remaining number of requests and the interval calculated from that.,

Total | 293 | 243

> If you need to restart the HA frequently, you must use other weather integration.
Sometimes there is a need, for frequent restarts, I do not do this regularly but when working out an integration that took more restarts than hoped for, there was no way around it.

The unplessant surprise was the rate limiting error for the AccuWeather integration. I think it is too easy to state that you then should not use AccuWeather. IMHO a component/integration should behave as best as it can and I think there is room for improvement here.

You could for instance not fire the request if the time window is not met upon restart and display a message that due to rate limiting data will not be fetched (yet), AFAIK there is already a timed interval to prevent hitting the rate limit.

> I am able to deduce the number of allowed requests per 24h

We have 50 allowed requests per day. Integration updates the data every 64 or 32 minutes depending on whether the forecast is enabled. This gives us 45 requests per day and 5 requests remain for HA restarts. In my opinion, this is a sufficient number. Determining how many requests are left is not a problem because we have this number from the `accuweather` library. The problem is to determine for how long this number of requests is provided.
Do you have an idea how to count the update interval when we don't know the reset time of the number of allowed requests?

> You could for instance not fire the request if the time window is not met upon restart and display a message that due to rate limiting data will not be fetched (yet), AFAIK there is already a timed interval to prevent hitting the rate limit.

Fetching data when HA is started is needed to check whether the service is online and whether the integration entities should be available. This is how `DataUpdateCoordinator` works in Home Assistant.

> I think there is room for improvement here.

As always, PR is most welcome.

Apart from that the headers from the reply even seem to contains the actual number of request allowed and remaining:


> As always, PR is most welcome.

I will see what I can do, not to familiar with the internals of Home Assistant yet.
If you figure out how to count the update interval, then I can prepare the PR.

> We have 50 allowed requests per day. Integration updates the data every 64 or 32 minutes depending on whether the forecast is enabled. This gives us 45 requests per day and 5 requests remain for HA restarts. In my opinion, this is a sufficient number. Determining how many requests are left is not a problem because we have this number from the `accuweather` library. The problem is to determine for how long this number of requests is provided.
> Do you have an idea how to count the update interval when we don't know the reset time of the number of allowed requests?

If there is 50 allowed requests per day I think the logic is not that hard:
1. After the initial request take not of the number of requests remaining.
2. Divide 24h * 3600s by the number of requests and you have the interval in seconds.
3. Next request repeats steps 1 and 2.

If the rate limit is reached you can see when you were able to perform the last successful request and do not request for 24h from that time, If we can find out the reset time of the API we could reduce the delay to that number.

Not sure if this is feasible in the Home Assistant architecture or this integration, but since you seem to be able to set the interval (judging from the options dialog in Home Assistant) I think it might be possible to do this dynamically.

> If the rate limit is reached you can see when you were able to perform the last successful request and do not request for 24h from that time, If we can find out the reset time of the API we could reduce the delay to that number.

The reset time is different for each API key.

> * After the initial request take not of the number of requests remaining.
> * Divide 24h * 3600s by the number of requests and you have the interval in seconds.
> * Next request repeats steps 1 and 2

Great idea, I had a completely different approach to this problem, your fresh approach was needed 😄 

EDIT:
After work I'll try to prepare the PR.

> Great idea, I had a completely different approach to this problem, your fresh approach was needed 😄

No problem, sometimes it helps to have a fresh look at things.



> After work I'll try to prepare the PR.

Great!

> * After the initial request take not of the number of requests remaining.
> * Divide 24h * 3600s by the number of requests and you have the interval in seconds.
> * Next request repeats steps 1 and 2.

However, this is not a good way because after each update the interval will be longer.
For example:
- after first update we have 50 requests so 1440 / 50 = 28 min
- after next update we have 49 requests so 1440 / 49  = 29 min
- after next update we have 48 requests so 1440 / 48  = 30 min

We still don't know when amount of requests will be reset.

This seems relevant to a feature request I put in yesterday and this issue highlights some suspicions about the API request limit reset time I had which would make my feature request challenging. Linking for reference. https://community.home-assistant.io/t/accuweather-allow-restricting-updates-to-certain-time-of-day/237832
The reset time is not fixed and is different for each user.

> The reset time is not fixed and is different for each user.

I doubt so, and apart from that you don't need to know the reset time. You can just rely on the data in the header and go from there. Intervals will be dynamic and change over time, but if done properly you should be within the rate limits and speed up when possible and slow down when needed.
Your fixed interval will be problematic if you consume more requests per 28m48s as you will reach the 50 allowed requests earlier, this happens for instance if you have one or more additional restarts of Home Assistant.

By making the interval dynamic and match it with the allowed number of requests you will limit the number of requests to the number of requests allowed and not hit the rate limit making it impossible to retrieve the data. You need to steer away of the fixed time limit for this to work.

You make a mistake in your calculations by forgetting to reduce the interval of 24h with the requests already consumed and their interval. If you factor these in you should see that you will keep a consistent interval.
By doing it like this it makes it possible to restart Home Assistant more often than 5 times as it will do a request, see the number of available requests and determine the interval.

At some time you will see that the number of allowed requests is higher than the previous time, that is the moment you should calculate the new interval and restart counting.

1. Do a request, record the number of requests allowed (`allowed_requests`) as well as the number of available requests (`available_requests`)
2. Calculate the interval by using the following formula: `interval = (24 * 60)/allowed requests`
3. Wait out the interval and do a next request
4. Compare the number of allowed requests with the initial value determined in step 1
  if higher, go to step 2 and proceed from there, if not higher go to step 3.

In (pseudo)code it would look something like this
```
interval = 0
previous_allowed_requests = 0
while True
    # Wait for the interval time to pass
    sleep interval

    response = request to API
    allowed_requests = response.header['allowed_requests']
    available_requests = response.header['available_requests']

    # Calculate the interval (after reset of the allowed requests or when first started)
    if allowed_requests > previous_allowed_requests:
        interval = (24 * 60)/allowed requests

    # Remember current value for next iteration
    previous_allowed_requests = allowed_requests

```

I really don't like this solution. I'll give you an example. If HA restarts when 5 requests remain, the update interval will be 360 ​​minutes and it will be used 5 times. So for 30 hours the weather data will be updated every 3 hours. There is no sense in the weather integration with data that is updated so rarely.

> I really don't like this solution. 

I am disappointed you do not see this as a better solution than your current one.

> I'll give you an example. If HA restarts when 5 requests remain, the update interval will be 360 ​​minutes and it will be used 5 times. 

Correct. This will give you at least some updated information during the period that you only have a limited number of requests available instead of yours providing a few relative quick updates and then no updates due to the limit being reached.

> So for 30 hours the weather data will be updated every 3 hours. There is no sense in the weather integration with data that is updated so rarely.

You are wrong here. It will continue to request at a low rate (every 6 hours/360minutes in your example) until AccuWeather API limit is reset (which will be 24 hours maximum and not 30h to the best of my knowledge), 
It will check this on every request if the limit is reset. As soon as the limit is reset (`allowed_request > previous_allowed_requests`) a new frequency will be calculated, which will probably be around 28m40s (24 * 60 / 50) again.

> I really don't like this solution. I'll give you an example. If HA restarts when 5 requests remain, the update interval will be 360 ​​minutes and it will be used 5 times. 

On second thought your calculations here are wrong as well. If you have five requests available over 24h the interval will be 24h * 60m / 5 = 288m (not 360m).

> On second thought your calculations here are wrong

Yes, I'm right, if you start with 5 requests, after first request you have:
`interval = 24 * 60 / 4`

> which will be 24 hours maximum and not 30h to the best of my knowledge

Yes, you are right, but for me, 30 or 24 hours makes no difference.
Your approach is wrong because you don't know how long the remaining requests must last. Maybe 5 requests left for hour, maybe 5 requests left for 10 hours.

> Yes, I'm right, if you start with 5 requests, after first request you have:
> `interval = 24 * 60 / 4`

No, I think you're not. You should divide by 5 and not by 4 as after 5 requests and an additional interval you will have a new batch of 50 requests, while your division by 4 puts your last request on the boundary where the reset should happen and 50 additional requests should be allowed, hopefully below table will make it a little clearer.

request|yours (min) |mine (min)
-|-|-
46|0|0
47|+360|+288
48|+720|+576
49|+1080|+864
50|+1440 (24h)|+1152
1|+1800|+1440 (24h)

> Your approach is wrong because you don't know how long the remaining requests must last. Maybe 5 requests left for hour, maybe 5 requests left for 10 hours

I think we will have to call it a draw as I don't think you will consider implementing my suggestion, where I consider you implementation suboptimal. 

I think my implementation it is more logical and friendly for users of Home Assistant to have information be available at a best effort instead of running out of requests and having a window without updated information. 

At least my suggestion provides updates throughout the possible window, perhaps in a lower frequency due to the throttling. but that is  due to the fact we cannot predict when the reset will be done. But as soon as the reset is done it will pick up at the speed that matches the number of allowed requests in the 24h time window.

Sorry, but I will not take the time to work on a solution that is incorrect in my opinion.
I believe that for weather integration, the maximum data download interval should be around 60 minutes.

> If you need to restart the HA frequently, you must use other weather integration.

@bieniu I like Accuweather, because this has the most accurate current weather report for my area, and the forecast also seems to be better than other solutions and I need the forecast for my morning TTS announcements (especially the precipitation probability, which some other weather integrations do not even have)

But recently I often had problem with exceeding the number of requests because playing with some settings, I have to restart HA few times a day.

What about giving an integration option to not requesting forecast in every query, but only in every nth request?
Having forecast updated at every 2 or even 3 hours would be still perfectly fine for me, with more than enough room to have some restarts a day.
I can add config option `less frequent updates` and with this option enabled `update_interval` will be 2 times longer.

That would be great, thanks!
For example today no data since the early morning restart, because yesterday I also had some restarts and it is unknown when will be the reset of my account.

I don't know the Accuweather API, so maybe a silly question, but  isn't it possible to alter query-by-query if you ask for forecast also or only current report?
Because forecast isn't too important to be updated frequently (I guess Accuweather itself does not update it too often as it requires many calculations) a few times a day is enough, so if forecast is the expensive query, most requests could be for current weather only, and only a few a day with forecast also.
But if you have to decide when initialising the API what kind of queries will you make, then this is out of question of course.

You must remember that your expectations may be different than the expectations of other users. Some prefer to update the forecast more often, others less frequently. The option to double the update interval is a good idea and should accommodate the needs of all users.
